approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds molecular graphs from a score-ranked population, using connected-fragment crossover and seven atom or bond mutations. It builds a fresh candidate pool, checks molecular identity and novelty, and rejects products that introduce an outside-envelope sulfur environment beyond the largest matching count in their original scored parents. A Gaussian process fitted to the complete current-session archive uses count fingerprints to draw correlated functions and select purchases. After three batches without an incumbent improvement, selection is restricted to the forty highest posterior means; improving feedback restores the full pool. Every accepted score enters the archive and greedy top-sixty-four survival determines future breeders. The Parent has already removed a dormant rejection-conditioned mutation escalation, while retaining ordinary multi-call mutation.
approach.novelty: Remove only the sulfur gate's power to reject a finished candidate, keeping its exact classifier and receipts as passive measurements. Every formerly rejected occurrence will enter the same pool update as another valid, novel candidate. This answers whether that retained restriction helps or harms the current stall-screened search. Earlier gate additions used a different host or a single-source walk; same-Parent siblings changed crossover, mutation continuation, features, posterior allocation, or the stall mask. The supplied sibling history contains no removal of this final sulfur-admission restriction. No endpoint sign or broad chemical benefit is assumed from the older gate results.

observed_bottleneck: The exact code Parent n-cf8d309c06de prevents its learned allocator from considering 138 otherwise valid canonically novel graph products. The new read-only audit of its declared Search panel finds 76,057 construction attempts: 69,600 pooled, 6,316 duplicate, 138 sulfur-rejected and 3 invalid; the sulfur classifier has 69,738 eligible opportunities. Positive excess occurs in 12/15 sessions and 78/435 batches, with 147 excess-signature units and 134 distinct session/identity pairs. Nineteen rejected attempts occur while the inherited stall restriction is requested. All 4,350 optimizer purchases and 2,175 late purchases are present; there are zero posterior fallbacks. The Parent mean is 0.607030316211131 with supplied population deviation 0.030175277546149237 and seed macros 0.649701282562401, 0.585233817344553, 0.586155848726439. Its own original-parent delta is exactly zero because its removed mutation floor was dormant; that earlier null does not price the exposed sulfur gate. The bottleneck is an unpriced admission restriction, not evidence that its rejected graphs would score well. The complete older L01 addition n-1744a1494180 gains only 0.0007834645552323346, with six favorable, six adverse and three tied cells on a mask-free host. L16 n-93cd9a000278/c-936b4670d5 has another reference/timing regime and a +0.005864965090889351 mean with seed-one loss -0.061423458899526995. n-814ee0b4f000 retained the gate while it blocked 236 coarse products, including 230 from five oxidized-sulfur entries; that is exposure, not this gate's contribution. Frozen catalog v-54264ad9a10c69d78e4f9470 therefore leaves m-93cd9a000278 unresolved on the current composition. Primary inputs and hashes are enumerated in policy/scratch/r0078-03-improve-L01/plan/evidence-review.json and its fifteen audit-seed files; these cite each original nodes/n-cf8d309c06de/seed-0, seed-1 and seed-2 summary.json, run.log, task log and trajectory file individually.

literature_review.conclusion: Apply only the preselected active-rejection removal while preserving the original sulfur classifier as an audit. The frozen review r78-window9-feedback-support-review and policy/scratch/search_policy-146d13ebf75c/literature-adoptions.json have been read; no new search is claimed and no literature source is adopted. Actual current-Parent rejections, exact source inspection, the frozen mechanism identity and the unmatched historical gate variants justify the isolated removal. None of the review's papers establishes this gate's endpoint sign or supplies a new algorithmic element for this ticket.

hypothesis: One isolated removal of the active final-pool rejection consumer of m-93cd9a000278 on n-cf8d309c06de. Preserve sulfur_envelope_permits, sulfur_outside_envelope_counts and sulfur_pool_introduction_audit exactly. For each exact outside-envelope signature h keep R(h)=max_p C_p(h) over the original actually selected scored generating parents, and D=sum_h max(C_candidate(h)-R(h),0). A multistep mutation uses its original scored source; crossover plus optional finishing mutation uses both original scored parents. At the existing boundary after checked_molecule, pool_identity_admission and the self.seen/pool_seen tests, compute and log the unchanged audit. Both D=0 and D>0 then proceed through the same existing pool_seen.add, pool.append, pooled counters, operator counters, pooled receipt and member_attempts reset. The legacy audit decision=reject means would-have-rejected only; it no longer controls admission. This exposes previously excluded support to the unchanged posterior allocation and, only if purchased and accepted, to the unchanged archive/survivor/breeding loop. The measured contribution is the total endpoint effect of removing that restriction, including refill/RNG-position, pool-covariance and later adaptive-history consequences. It is not a separately mediated effect of buying sulfur-containing molecules.

finding_summary.headline: Removing the sulfur gate raises the mean, although seven matched task endpoints decline
finding_summary.insights:
The admission restriction can affect this search substantially despite sparse direct purchases. Sitagliptin supplied the largest mean gain without buying a single positive-excess candidate or its descendant; this rules out an observed positive-excess purchased lineage as its explanation. Pool composition, refill stopping, covariance and later ordinary search histories all changed together, so the paired result prices the complete gate removal and does not identify a sulfur-mediated benefit. Ordinary sulfur-containing outputs actually decreased from 1,147 to 957, while nine outputs fell outside the narrow envelope. This is neither evidence for a blanket sulfur preference nor a general chemical-quality rule. The current-host contribution question is answered; transfer to other generators, the value of the retained measurement overhead and the usefulness of other chemical admission rules remain open.

The broader search limitation remains useful progress late in a session. Across the full 4,350 purchases, incumbent increments rose from 5.97807 to 6.07966, but across the 2,175 late purchases they fell from 1.02241 to 0.90202. Late parent beaters fell from 238 to 230, and 2,102 late purchases added no incumbent gain. The molecular audit finds broad overall scaffold variety, yet each task’s high-score subset occupies only 13–54 typed scaffolds and has fragment-excluded nearest-neighbour similarity of about 0.816–0.847. Both size tails persist, attachment liabilities remain frequent, and 2,532 molecules contain unassigned stereocentres with no explicit configurations. These observations support a limitation in finding and assessing useful alternative scaffold arrangements and attachment contexts, rather than an absence of sulfur, amines or ring-building capability. A different proposal operator coupled to a ranking model that can assess such rearrangements is the kind of method that could address that limitation; this removal does not establish its benefit or justify retuning an earlier recipe. The late decline and seven adverse cells remain part of the result, and the three paired seeds do not establish reliability.
finding_summary.results:
All 97 candidates with positive source-relative sulfur-signature excess entered the fresh pools, compared with 138 rejections by the Parent. The twelve exposed sessions matched their Parent histories until the first intended admission difference, and the three unexposed sessions reproduced completely. All fifteen sessions and 435 pools finished. Seven newly permitted candidates were purchased: six survived, four were reused as breeders, and three further accepted purchases descended from them. One direct purchase improved its incumbent by 0.04570; none of the fifteen final winners had this ancestry. Pool order changed in 272 batches and 2,650 purchase positions changed.

Mean endpoint score rose from 0.607030 to 0.613803, a paired gain of 0.006772. Seed changes were -0.009490, +0.016853 and +0.012954; five task/seed endpoints improved, seven declined and three tied. Mean task changes were -0.014353 for zaleplon, -0.009737 for decoration hopping, +0.012971 for DRD2, -0.010977 for median_2 and +0.055958 for sitagliptin. Macro population deviation fell from 0.030175 to 0.018714. The complete mean clears the registered +0.002 gain threshold with the formal Anchor as the actual code Parent, as well as the -0.002 noninferiority boundary. Under the registered descriptive contribution rule, retaining this active gate therefore had a negative conditional total endpoint contribution on this panel.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic series retain unusual halogen attachments and unspecified stereochemistry; nine outputs show unusual sulfur environments
molecular.overall_character: The Child produces predominantly medium-sized, aromatic, multiring graphs, including recognizable aryl amides, aza rings, ethers, carbonyls, thioethers and thiocarbonyls. Across 4,350 accepted optimizer observations, 4,249 have rings and 4,220 have aromatic atoms; the median is 28 heavy atoms and four perceived rings. The full heavy-atom range is 1–107, with 100 observations at six or fewer heavy atoms and 101 above 45. These coexist with nonstandard attachment patterns: 992 molecules contain N–halogen bonds, 215 O–halogen bonds, 278 single O–O bonds, 673 the defined aminal motif, and 49 carbon cumulenes. These overlapping structural flags warrant synthetic and stability scrutiny, but are not experimental impossibility or toxicity determinations. Neither this panel nor the Parent panel specifies tetrahedral or double-bond configuration under the identical RDKit procedure; the Child has 4,939 perceived unassigned centres in 2,532 molecules, compared with 4,392 in 2,578 Parent molecules. One Child molecule has explicit formal charges, a charge-separated nitrogen group; the rest are neutral representations. This does not mean that neutral amines cannot protonate. The full output contains 1,812 nonempty typed Murcko scaffolds and 1,081 generic scaffolds, versus 1,667 and 951 for the Parent. Mean within-session nearest-neighbour similarity after excluding fragments of six or fewer heavy atoms is 0.748739 versus 0.753118; diversity is present, while higher-scoring subsets still concentrate in related series. The comparison is complete for all fifteen Child/Parent task-seed cells, not merely a complete Child evaluation. Sulfur-containing observations fall from 1,147 in the Parent to 957 in the Child, although nine Child molecules versus zero Parent molecules contain an atom outside the exact archived neutral-sulfur envelope. Those nine include C#S attachments, hydrogen-bearing multiply bonded sulfur and N=S groups. Absolute output classification is not the source-relative admission statistic D and establishes neither gate activation nor sulfur-mediated benefit. N–halogen and O–halogen counts are 992/888 and 215/162 Child/Parent, single O–O counts are 278/118, while the small all-aromatic-ring flag falls from 170 to 25. The changing liabilities therefore do not support a single chemical-cleanliness direction. All counts exclude the ten fixed initial observations per session. RDKit 2023.09.6 default sanitized parsing is used identically for both arms, without tautomer or charge standardization. Stereo uses AssignStereochemistry(cleanIt=True, force=True) and FindMolChiralCenters(force=True, includeUnassigned=True, includeCIP=True, useLegacyImplementation=False); tagged atoms and definite double-bond stereo are counted separately. High/low subsets mean the highest/lowest 29 optimizer scores within each seed, with evaluation-order tie breaking, giving 87 observations per task; they are not a pooled decile dominated by one seed. Scaffolds use non-isomeric RDKit Murcko and MakeScaffoldGeneric; similarity uses achiral radius-two 2,048-bit Morgan fingerprints, excluding small fragments and comparing only within the same session. No synthetic-accessibility, conformational, stability, pKa or biological assay result was measured. No task is missing, no Parent trajectory is missing, and no held-out or Confirmation evidence was read. Child raw files are durable byte-identical Search snapshots of the frozen trusted worktree files, whose original absolute paths and hashes are preserved in policy/scratch/r0078-03-improve-L01/molecular/input-manifest.json. Counts and definitions are in policy/scratch/r0078-03-improve-L01/molecular/chemistry-summary.json and policy/scratch/r0078-03-improve-L01/molecular/molecule-descriptors.jsonl, with reproducible calculation in policy/scratch/r0078-03-improve-L01/molecular/measure.py. Frozen historical source hashes and variant limits are preserved in policy/scratch/r0078-03-improve-L01/molecular/history-review.json; the applicable sulfur identity is policy/catalog/versions/v-54264ad9a10c69d78e4f9470/catalog.json#mechanisms/m-93cd9a000278. Historical chemical associations do not identify a component effect. Every transferable gap below retains the current source and conditions and is a hypothesis about output capability, not evidence that a new hard filter will improve this benchmark.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 optimizer molecules have median 25 heavy atoms, range 1–47, and median three rings, predominantly aromatic. The leading seed-1 family joins an alkyl/methoxy-substituted fused aza-aromatic to a pyridyl carboxamide; both the ring nitrogen and amide nitrogen can carry halogen. Seed 0 instead ends with a more fused N–N-containing ring system bearing an N–OH group, while seed 2 has an indene-like carbon skeleton with two N-fluorinated carbonyl-linked nitrogens. Recognizable aryl carbonyl chemistry therefore coexists with unusual nitrogen attachments. The full set has 231 typed and 99 generic scaffolds; its high-score subset has 13 and nine. liabilities: 375 of 870 molecules have N–halogen bonds; ten have O–halogen and 18 single O–O bonds. Such local groups need stability and synthesis review even when the surrounding aromatic amide is familiar.
Twenty <=6-heavy-atom fragments and one >45-heavy-atom assembly are evaluated; 93 molecules have unassigned stereocentres and none specifies configuration.
The C#S attachment is outside the declared sulfur convention, but that convention alone does not prove the graph cannot exist.
missing_features: The output does not show consistently conventional attachment chemistry around its favored aromatic/carbonyl arrangement; the leading family retains N–halogen bonds rather than resolving that liability.

There is little high-score evidence outside a few related scaffold series, despite many full-trajectory scaffolds. No particular absent target pharmacophore or beneficial missing atom can be identified from these scores alone.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: C and C=COCl score zero, whereas CCc1c(OC)cc2c(cc(C(=O)N(Cl)c3ccccn3)n2F)c1C scores 0.46092619585962435. Changing the ring N–F to N–Br or N–Cl in the two quoted analogues gives exactly the same accepted score. This local gradient favors the retained aromatic/carbonyl arrangement over tiny fragments and is insensitive to those particular halogen identities; it does not demonstrate a preference for a more stable nitrogen substitution. N–halogen occurs in 62 of the 87 high-score observations versus 17 of the 87 low-score observations. The unusual C#S-containing output at seed 0/evaluation 87 scores 0.26976922072799436, below that session’s best; that single comparison cannot assign sulfur’s causal role. Child/Parent best-observed scores for seeds 0, 1, 2 respectively are 0.368468/0.423482, 0.460926/0.438799, 0.440334/0.450504.

transferable_gaps.gap: The observed generator does not consistently preserve conventional functional-group attachment environments when retaining otherwise recognizable aromatic and heterocyclic frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need to propose chemically coherent attachment alternatives that preserve a useful surrounding arrangement, while retaining the ability to represent legitimate unusual chemistry. Evaluate such alternatives through current-session accepted feedback; these output associations do not justify a universal element ban, a new chemical-quality objective, or repetition of an earlier refuted motif recipe. The sulfur classifier is a narrow convention, and neither its sign of contribution nor actual stability follows from these counts.

These are representation counts, not pKa or enantiomeric-purity measurements. Source measurements: policy/scratch/r0078-03-improve-L01/molecular/chemistry-summary.json.
transferable_gaps.gap: The observed output does not specify stereochemical state even when it builds stereogenic centres and multiple saturated ring junctions.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic representation and edit vocabulary would have to preserve or introduce explicit configurations, and distinguish state specification from connectivity, to explore that chemical degree of freedom. Charge-state variation would likewise require a chemically defined convention rather than an inference that every neutral drawing is uncharged in solution. The present trajectories provide no matched stereoisomer or protonation series, so no score benefit or binding preference for those states is established.

Using fixed heavy-atom tails of <=6 and >45, the Child has 100 small and 101 large optimizer observations, versus 98 and 79 in the Parent; the full ranges are 1–107 and 1–96. The smallest examples include isolated atoms and diatomics, and none of the five seed-stratified high-score subsets contains a <=6-atom molecule. The larger tail is not uniformly bad: one >45-atom molecule appears among those high-score subsets. These are diagnostic thresholds, not tested admission thresholds. Source measurements: policy/scratch/r0078-03-improve-L01/molecular/chemistry-summary.json.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably keep proposals within a structurally coherent size range; both tiny fragments and very large assemblies consume evaluations.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need constructive contraction and regrowth that can preserve connected ring and polar arrangements, rather than treating indiscriminate deletion or growth as sufficient exploration. Both size tails must remain visible when evaluating such a capability. The observations do not establish that a minimum-size cutoff, upper cap or blanket rejection improves the accepted-score search.

transferable_gaps.gap: Broad graph variety is present, but the highest-scoring observations still give limited evidence of escaping related decorated scaffold series.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The missing evidence is useful alternative scaffold arrangements with coherent attachment context, rather than more peripheral identity changes alone. A task-agnostic search could test whether it can sustain and assess such alternatives using its own feedback; neither scaffold diversity nor reduced similarity is itself a replacement objective or an established path to endpoint gain. Do not transfer a historical failed whole-fragment recipe merely because this output pattern persists.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
